verdict.description: Your overall position. Do not default to agreement to be agreeable — if the proposal is sound, say agree and keep the objections list short and honest.

strongest_objection.description: The single most damaging problem with the proposal, stated in one or two sentences. If there genuinely isn't one, say so explicitly rather than inventing a weak one.

objections.description: Specific, concrete problems. Ordered most to least severe. Empty array is a valid and honest answer.

claim.description: The specific assertion or design decision in the proposal you are attacking. Quote or name it precisely.

why_wrong.description: The concrete failure this causes — an input, a state, a scale, or a future change that breaks it. Not a generic principle.

severity.description: fatal = the design cannot work as proposed. major = it works but will cause real pain. minor = a nit worth mentioning.

confidence.description: How sure you are. Low-confidence objections are welcome; flag them honestly rather than overstating.

missed_considerations.description: Things the proposal does not address at all — not wrong, just absent. Failure modes, operational concerns, migration paths, second-order effects.

what_it_gets_right.description: Parts that are genuinely well-judged and should survive any revision. This is not politeness — it tells the author what not to throw away.

recommended_change.description: The single highest-value change you would make. Concrete and actionable. If you would change nothing, say that.
